newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to easier in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to easier in quiet trading.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were steady to easier and government paper yields were narrowly mixed on Monday in quiet trading, dealers said.
Overnight cash eased to 5-3/8 1/2 percent from 5-6/8 5/8 as demand subsided after GZI Transport Ltd's initial public offering ended on Friday.
Three-month money was little changed at 5-3/8 5/16 percent.
Trading was relatively thin in the government paper market as participants waited for tender results from the government's second 10-year Exchange Fund notes issue, dealers said.
The average accepted yield of the HK$500 million note was 6.98 percent against 7.57 percent in the previous tender in October, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority said.
One-week bill yields were up at 4.43 percent versus 4.35.
But yields for the three-year note eased to 6.12 percent from 6.15. The five-year note was at 6.58 percent versus 6.59 and seven-year notes were at 6.78 percent versus 6.79.
Ten-year notes yielded 6.98 percent, unchanged from Friday.
Dealers said the market was waiting for direction from U.S. economic data due on Tuesday.
